title: Peter the Great Works in a Dutch Shipyard
text:
In 1697 Tsar Peter I of Russia, then twenty-five years old, sent a large diplomatic mission, the Grand Embassy, to western Europe. Officially he was not part of it. He traveled incognito, under the name Peter Mikhailov, as a junior member. His real aim was to learn how western countries built ships and ran navies, which Russia lacked.

In August 1697 he went to Zaandam, a shipbuilding town in the Netherlands, and stayed in a small wooden house, which is preserved today. He worked in the yards for about a week before crowds of curious onlookers, who had soon worked out who he was, made it impossible.

He moved to Amsterdam, where he worked for about four months in the shipyard of the Dutch East India Company, taking part in building a frigate from the keel up, using the tools of a carpenter himself. He also visited workshops, hospitals and museums. He then went to England and studied at the royal dockyard at Deptford.

Peter returned to Russia with hundreds of recruited foreign specialists. He built a navy, founded Saint Petersburg in 1703 as a port on the Baltic, and pushed through sweeping reforms.
lesson: To change how others work, first learn the work yourself. Knowledge gained with your own hands earns respect and makes better decisions.
source: Accounts of the Grand Embassy; Dutch records at Zaandam and Amsterdam
